overview.text: The Eastern Coral Snake is a slender, brightly ringed elapid of the south-eastern United States. Its venom acts on the nervous system and is dangerous, but it is shy and secretive, and bites are very rare.

identification.text: Ringed with red, yellow and black around the whole body. In this species the red rings touch the yellow ones; a well-known rhyme ("red on yellow can kill a fellow") is based on that. Still, never rely on a rhyme to decide whether a snake is safe.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually less than 80 cm (31 in) in total length.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The south-eastern United States, including Florida - one of its other names is Florida Coral Snake.

habitat.text: Woodlands, pine and scrub forests, marshes and areas near water.

behaviour.text: Secretive and shy; it usually avoids people.

reproduction.text: Lays about three to 12 eggs in June, which hatch in September.
